NCT07527858 gives denikitug by intravenous infusion alone, with nivolumab, or with trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab, against trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab alone. Its CMS Part D beneficiaries were 147 in 2023, 1,935 in 2024 (annual file 7e0b4365-fd63-4a29-8f5e-e0ac9f66a81b) and 2,203 in 2025 (quarterly file 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15), up 14% in its second full year, so 2025 is near its plateau. In 2025 it was 24.72% of the refractory orals' Part D beneficiaries: 2,203 of 2,203 + 4,784 (Lonsurf) + 1,925 (Stivarga) = 8,912 (25.45% in 2024: 1,935 of 7,604). In the Nevala-Plagemann cohort the 4,407 third-line patients took 2,147 courses of the refractory orals (1,937 patients, 111 of them regorafenib after trifluridine-tipiracil and 99 the reverse), 0.4872 a patient. 0.2472 x 0.4872 = 12.04% of the third-line cohort on fruquintinib. With the pool equal to its inflow the engine carries no untreated patient forward, so the peak is the long-run share of each year's cohort. MULTIPLE 1.0: no judgement is laid on the analogue. For more: one arm adds denikitug to the refractory standard rather than replacing it. Against: CCR8 depletion has shown no colorectal efficacy yet, and the study is a Phase 2 on response rate
